sample_unit: Reddit comments (120 threads, eight clinician subreddits)

links.outcome: Clinician perceptions of accountability for AI-generated note errors
links.effect: Thematic analysis of 484 comments found an accountability vacuum in which the clinician signature acts as a legal shock absorber for institutional AI liability.
links.quote: First, an accountability vacuum exists where the mandatory clinician signature functions merely as a legal shock absorber for institutional AI liability.

links.outcome: Clinician perceptions of hallucinations in AI-generated notes
links.effect: Clinicians framed AI hallucinations as a mathematically inevitable epistemic risk rather than a correctable technical bug (qualitative theme, no rates reported).
links.quote: Second, clinicians frame AI hallucinations as a mathematically inevitable epistemic risk rather than a correctable technical bug.

links.outcome: Clinician concerns about upcoding and over-documentation from AI scribes
links.effect: Clinicians described AI-driven over-documentation and productivity demands as threatening the fiscal credibility of the record through inadvertent upcoding (qualitative theme).
links.quote: Finally, institutional productivity demands and AI-driven over-documentation severely threaten the fiscal credibility of the medical record through inadvertent upcoding.

unlisted_practices: contingent transparency mechanisms for provenance tracking of AI-generated note text
patient-facing error contestation mechanisms for AI-generated notes in OpenNotes

screen.reason: The study conducts a qualitative thematic analysis of clinician discourse regarding the real-world use, governance, and accountability challenges of ambient AI documentation tools in the OpenNotes era.
